# Temple Scroll Column 53 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 53 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 53:1 — "come into" vs. "enter" vs. "be admitted to"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shall not come into the assembly" | Literal yavo' — standard Hebrew verb of entry |
| LOGOS | "shall enter the assembly" | Standard English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "shall be admitted to the assembly" | Passive construction emphasizing the gatekeeping function |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "enter" (LOGOS). Simple and direct; "admitted" implies a bureaucratic process not present in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 53:8 — "night-occurrence" vs. "nocturnal emission" vs. "bodily emission during the night"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "night-occurrence" | Literal miqreh laylah — preserves the Hebrew euphemism |
| LOGOS | "nocturnal emission" | Standard medical/scholarly term that clarifies the euphemism |
| PNEUMA | "bodily emission during the night" | Explanatory rendering for readers unfamiliar with the term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "nocturnal emission" (LOGOS). It is precise, universally understood, and standard in biblical scholarship.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 53:12 — "thing of nakedness" vs. "anything indecent" vs. "anything offensive"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a thing of nakedness" | Literal ervat davar — the same phrase used in Deut 24:1 for grounds of divorce |
| LOGOS | "anything indecent" | Standard rendering capturing the sense of impropriety |
| PNEUMA | "anything offensive" | Broader modern term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "anything indecent" (LOGOS). "Thing of nakedness" is too literal for English; "offensive" (PNEUMA) is too vague and loses the specific connotation of physical/moral impropriety.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 53:15 — "holy-woman/holy-man" vs. "cult prostitute" vs. "temple prostitute"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "holy-woman... holy-man" | Literal qedeshah/qadesh — preserving the ironic use of the root q-d-sh ("holy") |
| LOGOS | "cult prostitute" | Standard scholarly rendering identifying the sacral-sexual function |
| PNEUMA | "temple prostitute" | Specifies the institutional setting |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "cult prostitute" (LOGOS). EMET's "holy-woman" is profoundly misleading in English. PNEUMA's "temple prostitute" implies a specific building, while "cult prostitute" correctly identifies the religious context without over-specifying.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 53:16 — "price of a dog" — literal vs. interpretive

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the price of a dog" | Literal Hebrew kelev — the term is retained without interpretation |
| LOGOS | "the price of a dog" | Same; retained literally with note that it likely denotes a male cult prostitute |
| PNEUMA | "the earnings of a male prostitute" | Interprets the metaphorical referent directly |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted the literal "price of a dog" (EMET/LOGOS). The meaning is debated among scholars; interpretation should be left to footnotes rather than embedded in the translation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
